questions.question: Explain how to draw a pie chart from percentage data.
questions.expected_answer: The whole circle represents 100% and 360 degrees; multiply each percentage by 3.6 to get its angle (e.g. 50% = 180 degrees, 25% = 90 degrees, 10% = 36 degrees); draw a circle with a compass, draw a starting radius, measure each angle with a protractor in turn (usually largest first, clockwise); shade/colour each sector; add a key or labels with percentages, a title and the data source.

questions.question: Describe the main users of water in South Africa and their approximate shares.
questions.expected_answer: Irrigation/agriculture about 60% (fruit, vegetables, sugar cane, wheat, citrus, wine grapes along the Orange, Vaal, Breede, Olifants rivers); municipal about 27% (homes, businesses, schools, hospitals); afforestation about 3%; industry about 3.5%; mining about 2.5%; power generation about 2%; livestock and conservation about 2%. Irrigation's sector is about 216 degrees on a pie chart, more than half.

questions.question: How does the National Water Act aim to share water fairly, and how can water be used more wisely?
questions.expected_answer: Water belongs to the nation, held in trust by government (not tied to land ownership as before 1994); the reserve - basic human needs and ecological reserve - has priority; other users need licences; Free Basic Water (6000 litres per household per month). Wiser use: fix leaks (municipal losses about 40%), drip and efficient irrigation, reuse treated waste water, harvest rainwater, water-wise indigenous gardens, clear alien plants, save water at home and school.
